Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the incredible journey you've been on, becoming a new mother. It's a time of great joy, but also significant adjustment, and it's completely normal to experience a range of emotions. 

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us understand how you're feeling and to identify any areas where we might be able to offer additional support. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional well-being and to make sure you're getting the care you need.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and is a safe space for you to express yourself honestly. I'm here to listen and support you, without judgment. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. We'll go through each question together, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and supportive as possible.

Let's get started. The first question I'd like to ask is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or down?

.. to be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle. I mean, I'm so grateful to have my baby, and I love her so much, but taking care of her is just exhausting. I feel like I'm running on empty most of the time. Some days are better than others, but lately, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and anxious about everything. I worry about her health, and whether I'm doing everything right... it's just a lot of pressure. 

As for enjoying things I usually like to do... I don't really have the time or energy for that right now. I used to love reading and taking walks, but those things seem like a luxury I don't have time for anymore. Even simple things, like taking a shower or getting dressed, feel like a chore. But, at the same time, I do get happy moments with my baby, like when she smiles at me or falls asleep in my arms... those moments make everything feel worth it. It's just... it's hard to explain, I guess. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than really living it. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still have moments where I can laugh and joke with my partner or family, but it's not as frequent as it was before the baby was born. Most of the time, I'm just so tired and preoccupied with taking care of her that I don't really have the energy to think about funny things or find the humor in situations. And when I do try to laugh or joke, it sometimes feels forced, like I'm just going through the motions. 

But, like I said, there are moments with my baby that make me happy and even laugh - like when she makes these adorable little faces or coos at me. Those moments are really special, and they make all the hard work worth it. It's just... it's hard to feel like myself right now, you know? I feel like I'm just trying to get by, rather than really enjoying life. (pausing, looking a bit down) Sorry, I don't know if that makes sense... it's just been really tough lately.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head slightly) Not really, to be honest. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it's just hard to think about anything beyond the next feeding or diaper change. Everything feels so overwhelming, and I'm just trying to get through each day. I don't really have the energy or motivation to think about fun things to do or look forward to them.

Even simple things, like meeting a friend for coffee or going for a walk, feel like a huge production now. I have to worry about the baby's schedule, and whether I can get her to sleep, and whether I can even get out of the house on time... it's just too much. And most of the time, I end up canceling plans or putting things off because I just don't feel up to it.

It's not that I don't want to enjoy things or look forward to them... it's just that everything feels so hard right now. And when I do try to think about fun things, I just feel anxious about how I'm going to make it all work with the baby. (sighing) I feel like I've lost my sense of excitement and anticipation, and it's just been replaced with worry and exhaustion.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding slightly) Yeah, I do that sometimes. I mean, when the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, or when I'm not producing enough milk, or when I'm just feeling really overwhelmed... I tend to beat myself up over it. I think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I do this? I'm a bad mom..." It's like, I know it's not rational, but it's hard not to take it personally when things aren't going well.

And it's not just the big things, either. Sometimes it's just little things, like if I forget to pack a diaper in the diaper bag, or if I run out of formula... I'll think to myself, "How could I be so stupid? What kind of mom forgets that?" It's like, I'm already feeling so anxious and unsure of myself, and then I make a little mistake, and it just feels like confirmation that I'm not cut out for this.

But, at the same time, I try to remind myself that everyone makes mistakes, and that it's okay not to be perfect. It's just hard to shake that feeling of self-doubt and guilt, you know? (looking down, fidgeting slightly) I feel like I'm just trying to do my best, but it never feels like it's good enough.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding, looking concerned) Oh, yeah... that's been happening a lot lately. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? What if I'm not doing something right? What if she gets sick? It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I get this knot in my stomach... it's really overwhelming.

And the thing is, it's not even like there's a specific reason for me to be worried. The pediatrician says the baby is healthy, and we're doing everything right... but I just can't shake this feeling of anxiety. It's like, I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop, or something. (bites lip)

Sometimes it's hard to sleep at night, too, because I'll be lying there thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? What if there's a fire in the house? It's just... it's really hard to calm my mind down and relax. (looks up, eyes wide with concern) Does that sound crazy? Am I just being paranoid?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. It's like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart starts racing, and I feel like I'm going to hyperventilate... it's really scary. And the thing is, it's not even like there's anything specific that's triggering it. I'll just be going about my day, taking care of the baby, and then suddenly I'll feel like I'm going to lose control or something.

It's hard to describe, but it's like my body just takes over and I feel like I'm in fight-or-flight mode or something. I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel like I'm just waiting for disaster to strike. It's a really overwhelming feeling, and it's hard to shake it off once it starts.

Sometimes, when it happens, I'll try to distract myself by doing something else, like taking a warm bath or listening to calming music. But other times, it's just too much, and I'll end up in tears. (looks down, fidgeting with hands) It's just really frustrating, because I feel like I should be able to control my emotions, you know? I'm a mom now, and I'm supposed to be strong and capable... but sometimes I just feel like I'm barely holding it together.

(pauses, taking a deep breath) I guess what I'm trying to say is that it's not just anxiety or worry, it's like... it's a physical feeling, too. My body feels like it's on high alert all the time, and it's exhausting. (looks up, eyes searching for understanding) Does that make sense?
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly running on a treadmill and getting nowhere. I'm tired all the time, but I never seem to get a break. Even when my partner tries to help, I still feel like I'm shouldering all the responsibility.

And it's not just the baby, it's everything else too. The house is a mess, I'm not cooking or cleaning like I used to, and I feel like I'm neglecting my relationship with my partner. I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water, and if one more thing gets added to my plate, I'm going to sink.

I try to prioritize and make lists and all that, but it's hard to keep up. And sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a competent mom, you know? Like, I'm just faking it until I make it, but really I have no idea what I'm doing. (looks down, voice dropping to a whisper) It's scary, because I feel like I'm not doing enough, and that the baby is going to suffer because of it.

(looks up, eyes welling up with tears) Sorry, I'm just... it's just really hard right now. I feel like I'm drowning in all these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (takes a deep breath, trying to compose herself) I guess that's why I'm here, right? To try to figure out how to make it all work?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, looking tired) Yeah, that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. I mean, that's part of it, but even when she's sleeping, I'm not. I'll lie there and my mind will just start racing, thinking about all the things I need to do, and worrying about whether I'm doing everything right. And then I'll start feeling anxious and overwhelmed, and it's just hard to calm down.

Some nights, I'll be awake for hours, just lying there and staring at the ceiling. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm exhausted, but I'm also... I don't know, it's like my body is just on high alert all the time, waiting for the next thing to go wrong.

It's not just the lack of sleep, though. It's the feeling of unhappiness, too. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just... everything feels so hard right now. And I feel like I'm not enjoying it as much as I should be. I feel like I'm just struggling to get through each day, rather than actually living it. (sighs, looking down) It's a really sad feeling, you know? Like, I'm missing out on all the joy and happiness that I'm supposed to be feeling as a new mom.

(looks up, eyes searching for understanding) Does that make sense? Am I just... am I just being a bad mom, or is this normal? (voice cracks, and she looks like she's on the verge of tears)
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes) Yeah, that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, taking care of the baby and doing all the things I'm supposed to do, but inside, I'm just feeling so... empty. And sad. And overwhelmed. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And I'll start crying, and I won't be able to stop.

It's not all the time, though. Sometimes I'll have good days, where I feel like I'm actually enjoying being a mom, and I'll laugh and play with the baby, and it'll feel like everything is okay. But then the next day, or the next hour, I'll be back to feeling sad and miserable again. It's like, I'm just on this rollercoaster of emotions, and I don't know how to get off.

I feel like I'm grieving, too. Grieving the life I had before the baby, and the person I used to be. I know that's not a bad thing, having a baby and all, but it's just... it's hard to let go of who I was, and to adjust to this new reality. And sometimes, when I'm feeling really down, I'll think about how I used to be, and how I used to feel, and it'll just make me feel even sadder.

(looks down, wiping away tears) I'm sorry, I'm just... it's just really hard right now. I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, and grateful, and all those things, but inside, I'm just feeling really lost and alone. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I guess that's why I'm here, though. To try to figure out how to feel better, and how to be a good mom, even when it's hard.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes again) Yeah, that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I've been crying all the time, and it's not just when the baby is crying, or when I'm tired, or when things are going wrong. It's just... it's like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sadness, and I'll start crying. And it's not just a little bit of crying, either. It's like, I'll be sobbing, and I won't be able to stop.

Sometimes, I'll be crying, and my partner will try to comfort me, and I'll just push them away. I don't mean to, it's just... I feel like I'm so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to explain it, or how to make it stop. And sometimes, I'll be crying, and the baby will be crying, too, and it's just... it's like, I feel like I'm failing, you know? Like, I'm not doing enough, or I'm not doing it right, and it's just... it's really hard.

(looks down, wiping away tears) I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's not just about the baby, or being a mom. It's about... it's about everything. It's about feeling lost, and alone, and overwhelmed. It's about feeling like I'm not good enough, or that I'm not doing enough. And it's about feeling like I'm just... I'm just stuck, you know? Like, I don't know how to get out of this place, or how to make it better.

(takes a deep breath, trying to compose herself) I'm sorry, I'm just... it's just really hard right now. I feel like I'm crying all the time, and I don't know how to stop. (pauses, looking up) But I guess that's why I'm here, right? To try to figure out how to feel better, and how to be a good mom, even when it's hard.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head vigorously) No, no, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and like I don't know how to keep going, but hurting myself is not something that's ever crossed my mind. I'm just trying to get through each day, and take care of my baby, and figure out how to be a good mom. I don't think about harming myself, I just think about... (pauses, looking for the right words) I just think about feeling better, and being happy again, and enjoying my baby. That's all I want.

(looks up, eyes serious) I want to make it clear that I would never hurt myself. I'm just trying to get help, and figure out how to feel better, because I want to be a good mom, and take care of my baby. I want to be happy, and enjoy this time with my baby, and I know that I need some help to get there. (pauses, taking a deep breath) I'm glad I'm here, and I'm glad I can talk about this stuff. It's just... it's really hard, you know? Being a mom is hard, and it's okay to admit that, and to ask for help.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient, a new mother, presents with several symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. The main symptoms expressed include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of pleasure in activities
* Difficulty sleeping due to overwhelming thoughts and anxiety
* Frequent crying spells
* Feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-doubt
* Anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Difficulty coping with responsibilities and adjusting to new role as a mother

Consistent patterns across answers include low mood, loss of enjoyment, and anxiety. The patient reports feeling overwhelmed, struggling to care for her baby, and experiencing significant emotional distress.

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression and anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and being overwhelmed

Specific risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and crying spells
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety and panic
* Difficulty coping with responsibilities and adjusting to new role as a mother

Notably, the patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, which is a positive indicator of safety.

**Screening Observation Summary:**

This new mother presents with a constellation of symptoms and emotional concerns suggestive of postpartum depression and anxiety. Her reports of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, combined with feelings of worthlessness and guilt, indicate a need for further evaluation and potential support. The patient's difficulty sleeping, frequent crying spells, and struggles with coping and adjustment to her new role as a mother also warrant attention. While the patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, her overall presentation suggests a need for careful monitoring and potential intervention to support her mental health and well-being.
